keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1971-1972, before Cliopatria's row (1973): 'On 3 September 1971, under an agreement with the UK, the special treaty arrangements were terminated' (infobox: independence 3 September 1971). The shape is Cliopatria's 1973 shape.

12,778 km2 for 1973-2023 against the infobox's 11,581 km2 (ratio 1.10; no year on the figure). The gazetteer resolves the shape to 48 cells, one (253 km2) beyond Natural Earth's Qatar. Zubarah on the north-west coast is inside it; the Hawar Islands and Fasht al-Dibal are not (the ledger gives Fasht al-Dibal and Janan to Qatar in 2001).
12,778 km2, the same outline for 2024 (ratio 1.10). No border change on the page for the final year.

ledger.note: 3 September 1971: Qatar becomes independent. 'On 3 September 1971, under an agreement with the UK, the special treaty arrangements were terminated'; the protectorate dated from the treaty of 3 November 1916 with Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani.

ledger.note: April 1986: Qatar acts on Fasht al-Dibal. 'Qatar sends security force to put an end to construction work undertaken by Bahrain on then-disputed' Fasht al-Dibal (April 1986); Qatar filed at the ICJ in July 1991 to overturn 'the 1939 British decision to award the islands to Bahrain'.

Fasht al-Dibal, the reef where Bahrain was building in 1986

ledger.note: March 2001: the International Court of Justice rules. 'March 2001: Qatar v. Bahrain Maritime Delimitation and Territorial Questions (Merits) judgement is delivered'; the Court 'awarded Zubarah to Qatar on the basis of the Anglo-Ottoman Convention of 1913'.
March 2001: Qatar wins Fasht al-Dibal. The Court awarded Qatar Zubarah 'as well as Fasht al-Dibal'. Zubarah was already Qatar's ground and only the reef changes hands.

ledger.note: 2001: Qatar wins Janan Island. The Hawar Islands page, on the dispute 'resolved in 2001' (judgment of 16 March 2001): Janan 'was awarded to Qatar'. The Qatar v. Bahrain page is silent on Janan.

wars.outcome: After the Fasht al-Dibal incident of April 1986 and Qatar's filing at the ICJ in July 1991, the Court's judgment of March 2001 gave Qatar Zubarah, Fasht al-Dibal and Janan, and Bahrain 16 of the 17 Hawar elements and Qit'at Jaradah.
wars.note: A legal and naval dispute, not a war. The Qatar page is silent on the Hawar dispute, the 1986 clash and the 2001 ruling.

wars.name: Qatar diplomatic crisis
wars.outcome: In June 2017 Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain, Egypt and Yemen broke diplomatic ties with Qatar; the crisis ended with the al-Ula declaration in January 2021. No territory changed.
wars.note: The page does not use the word blockade. Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered.

certainty.note: The Hawar Islands, Fasht al-Dibal and Zubarah were disputed with Bahrain; the page says nothing about the land frontier with Saudi Arabia (Qatar's only land border) so it is not read as a surveyed line.
The ICJ judgment of March 2001 fixed the Qatar-Bahrain title; the Saudi land border is still not described by any page opened.

notes: Written by me-10-l on 2026-10-25 from three pages (one over the 1-2 page budget: the Hawar Islands page was opened to settle Janan). SHARED WIKIDATA Q846 with qatar-dynasty (Cliopatria 1820-1904), qatar (Sheikhdom of Qatar 1913-1916) and, through its own dossier, qatar-protectorate (1916-1971): four dossiers of one state in turn, the colour agent may keep one hue. This one starts at independence on 3 September 1971; Cliopatria's row starts in 1973, hence the new 1971 keyframe. THE QATAR PAGE IS SILENT on the Hawar Islands, the 1986 clash, the 2001 ruling, Zubarah's award, the Saudi border (1965 agreement, 1992 Khafous incident, 1999-2001 agreement), so every territorial event rests on the Qatar v. Bahrain and Hawar Islands pages. Khor al Adaid is mentioned only historically (Abu Dhabi occupied it before an expedition of 1882). RULERS: Ahmad bin Ali's accession year is not on the page; the strip starts at independence. NAMES FOR THE GAZETTEER: Hawar Islands (region), Fasht ad Dibal, Janan Island (places).
